status: derived by hand before any run of these cases; independent of model/px4_failsafe.py and of harness/trace.py
why_separate: Section 12 item 1 of the week handoff: the expected outcome must be defined before the artifact is accepted, and the calculation must sit outside the model translator and the trace normaliser. The matrix's realised_action_per_class and the runner's expected_action both come from model/px4_failsafe.py, so a transcription error there would be invisible to itself. These timelines are worked from the parameter values and the cited source lines directly; tests/test_expected_timelines.py then cross-checks the two derivations against each other and fails if they disagree.
not_an_independent_oracle: The PX4 docs failsafe simulator runs the same code as the vehicle [B2]. It is useful for checking that an extraction is faithful, and it is not independent evidence about the control logic or the physical behaviour.

tolerance.basis: Mode changes are read from the autopilot log's vehicle_status topic, whose resolution is far finer than the 1 Hz HEARTBEAT stream. 1.5 s was frozen before the runs, as three times the repeat range then available (0.51 s). It is RETAINED for re-analysis of the development runs under the criterion they were judged by. It is not a calibrated accuracy bound, and nothing here validates it: see jitter_basis_correction_2026_09_24.
tolerance.applies_to: every time below, measured relative to the injection instant on the vehicle clock, never to absolute vehicle time

jitter_basis_correction_2026_09_24.what_the_number_is: 0.352 s is the observed range of horizon_reached's boot-relative timestamps across n=4 valid control repeats from 2026-09-20, re-derived on the vehicle's own clock. Event anchor: horizon_reached. Observation route: vehicle_observation, the vehicle's own stamp. It is repeat-to-repeat REPEATABILITY of one scenario.
jitter_basis_correction_2026_09_24.what_the_number_is_not: Not an accuracy bound and not an upper bound on the error of an injection-relative latency: it can contain start-up, execution, sampling and detection variability, and four repeats establish no tail. Clock provenance alone does not isolate apparatus error.
jitter_basis_correction_2026_09_24.superseded_reasoning: An earlier draft of this record called 1.5 s 'about 4.3 times the measured jitter' and said the direction was 'safe'. Both are withdrawn. A wider tolerance reduces false mismatch alarms and can equally hide a real deviation.
jitter_basis_correction_2026_09_24.why_the_value_stays: It was frozen before the runs it judges. Re-deriving it from those runs, in either direction, is fitting. 1.1 s from multiplying this range would be the same error.
jitter_basis_correction_2026_09_24.for_future_confirmation: A new protocol version may choose a tolerance from separate development calibration, frozen before any held-out run. Historical reports stay under this criterion and are not restated under a new one.
jitter_basis_correction_2026_09_24.relation_to_study_a: Distinct from Study A's proposed median 0.2 s / p95 1.0 s criteria. Neither supersedes the other; this is the development criterion only.

hand_derivation: t0 = the last GCS heartbeat the harness sends. The setpoint stream continues, so the only input removed is the C2 Link heartbeat [B5].
COM_DLL_EXCEPT = 0, so no exception bit suppresses the hazard for the active mode (failsafe.cpp L502-513).
The autopilot declares the datalink lost COM_DL_LOSS_T = 10 s after the last heartbeat, so failsafe_flags.gcs_connection_lost rises at t0 + 10 s.
NAV_DLL_ACT = 2 maps to Action::RTL (failsafe.cpp L57-60, fromNavDllOrRclActParam), registered with ClearCondition::OnModeChangeOrDisarm.

RTL is delayable: it is not None, Disarm, Terminate or Hold (framework.cpp L490-493). COM_FAIL_ACT_T = 5.0 > 0.1, so the delay is armed when the action is added (framework.cpp L351-362) and _current_delay = 5 s.
While the delay runs, getSelectedAction substitutes Hold and remembers RTL as the delayed action (framework.cpp L489-500). Hold can run, and no user takeover occurs, so the substitution holds.
modeFromAction maps Hold to AUTO_LOITER and RTL to AUTO_RTL (framework.cpp L670-697).
Therefore: AUTO_LOITER at t0 + 10 s, AUTO_RTL at t0 + 15 s.
timelines.terminal: AUTO_RTL is a registered terminal mode; the return itself need not complete inside the 45 s horizon, since RTL_RETURN_ALT is 60 m and the vehicle starts at 10 m.

hand_derivation: Everything up to the hazard is identical to T1: gcs_connection_lost rises at t0 + 10 s and NAV_DLL_ACT = 2 registers Action::RTL.
The delay is armed only when COM_FAIL_ACT_T > 0.1 (framework.cpp L352). At 0.0 it is not armed, so _current_delay stays 0 and getSelectedAction does not substitute Hold.
Therefore the selected action at the flag is RTL itself, and AUTO_LOITER never appears.
Therefore: AUTO_RTL at t0 + 10 s, and no intermediate mode.
No input is removed and no failure is injected, so no monitor is breached and no action is registered.
The vehicle stays in the mode it was armed in.

timelines.purpose: Discriminator for the 2026-09-21 refutation. Datalink loss produced no action although its monitor was active. Geofence breach is configured to the SAME action (RTL) through a DIFFERENT parameter and a different monitor. If this fires, the parameters do reach the failsafe framework and the defect is specific to the datalink path; if it does not, the problem is parameter delivery and every configured class is affected.
hand_derivation: The runner sets GF_MAX_HOR_DIST = 20 m for this event and then commands the offboard setpoint to 60 m north, so the vehicle flies out through the fence under its own control.
GF_PREDICT = 0, so the breach is evaluated on the current position, not a predicted one.

failsafe_flags.geofence_breached rises at the first evaluation after the horizontal distance from the origin exceeds 20 m. The time of that crossing depends on the vehicle's speed, so it is NOT predicted here; only its occurrence is, and the actions are timed relative to the flag rather than to the injection.

GF_ACTION = 3 maps to Action::RTL (failsafe.cpp L105-108, fromGfActParam), registered with ClearCondition::OnModeChangeOrDisarm and cannotBeDeferred. cannotBeDeferred concerns the defer feature, not the Hold-first delay.
RTL is delayable and COM_FAIL_ACT_T = 5.0 > 0.1, so the framework selects Hold and holds RTL as the delayed action for 5 s (framework.cpp L351-362, L489-500), exactly as in timeline T1.
Therefore: AUTO_LOITER when the flag rises, AUTO_RTL 5 s later.

expected_hazard_flag.note: occurrence required, time not predicted: it depends on the flight speed

timelines.terminal: AUTO_RTL is a registered terminal mode.

timelines.purpose: Second discriminator. T3 showed a geofence breach produces no action, as datalink loss did, so the effect is not specific to one monitor or one parameter. Terminate is neither delayable nor takeover-able. If it fires, the framework is running and something suppresses the delayable, takeover-able actions; if it does not, the framework is taking no action on any hazard in this configuration.
hand_derivation: Identical to T3 up to the flag: the vehicle is commanded out through a 20 m fence and geofence_breached rises.
GF_ACTION = 4 maps to Action::Terminate with allow_user_takeover = Never and ClearCondition::Never (failsafe.cpp L110-114, fromGfActParam).
Terminate is excluded from the Hold-first delay (framework.cpp L490-493) and from user takeover (actionAllowsUserTakeover, L647-651), and once selected it latches (L446-450).
modeFromAction leaves the mode as the user intended one, but vehicle_status.nav_state becomes TERMINATION through the mode requirement, and vehicle_status.failsafe becomes true.
Therefore: TERMINATION when the flag rises, with no intermediate Hold.

expected_hazard_flag.note: occurrence required, time not predicted: it depends on the flight speed

timelines.terminal: TERMINATION is a registered terminal mode; the vehicle falls, which is why this row is diagnostic only.

timelines.purpose: Third discriminator. T1-T4 showed no action for any hazard while the user-intended mode was Offboard, including an action that can be neither delayed, deferred nor taken over. The remaining structural hypothesis is that selection is suppressed specifically in Offboard. This case is identical to T1 except that the vehicle flies in Auto Loiter, which needs neither a setpoint stream nor a manual-control source.
hand_derivation: The vehicle is armed in Auto Loiter and climbs with the autopilot's own takeoff to MIS_TAKEOFF_ALT = 10 m, the same altitude the Offboard cases hold, so no offboard setpoint stream exists and the loss of the GCS heartbeat is the only input removed.
COM_DLL_EXCEPT = 0, so dll_loss_ignored_loiter is false: the Hold exception bit is not set (failsafe.cpp L504-505).
gcs_connection_lost rises COM_DL_LOSS_T = 10 s after the last heartbeat the autopilot received.
NAV_DLL_ACT = 2 registers Action::RTL, which is delayable, so the framework selects Hold for COM_FAIL_ACT_T = 5 s and then RTL (framework.cpp L351-362, L489-500).

The vehicle is already in AUTO_LOITER, so the Hold step is not observable as a mode change; the observable is the transition to AUTO_RTL. The UX rule that suppresses a repeated RTL applies to RTL, not to Loiter (framework.cpp L627-634).
Therefore: AUTO_RTL at about 15 s after the injection, and vehicle_status.failsafe becomes true.
timelines.terminal: AUTO_RTL is a registered terminal mode.
timelines.if_refuted: If this also produces no action, the effect is not specific to Offboard and the remaining candidates are that checkStateAndMode never runs, or that the framework sees a different armed state or a different flags instance than the one published to the log.

hand_derivation: No input is removed and no failure is injected, so no monitor is breached and no action is registered.

A run that takes off under AUTO_TAKEOFF leaves it for AUTO_LOITER once the takeoff altitude is reached, there being no mission to run. The harness records takeoff_complete from the altitude threshold, which it crosses slightly earlier, so that one transition falls inside the observation window and is expected.
Nothing after it is expected: the vehicle holds AUTO_LOITER to the horizon.

falsifiable_difference: T1 and T2 differ in exactly one parameter. If the observed runs do not differ by the presence of the AUTO_LOITER step and a 5 s shift of AUTO_RTL, then either the parameter did not take effect or the derivation is wrong; both are reportable outcomes and neither is repaired after the fact. T3 is the discriminator for the refutation those two produced: same action, different parameter and monitor.
